note: P3923 (Pro 11:22) — like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman without discretion. (aph 'snout' left as image, not IB.)

dims.v: indiscretion — beauty that turns from good sense
the turning-from/lack of discretion that makes beauty grotesque
(the incongruous gold ring in a snout)
the absent discretion that renders beauty absurd

sur (turn aside/depart) — 'a beautiful woman WITHOUT (turned from) discretion'; outward beauty voided by the lack of inner taste/discretion, as incongruous as gold in a pig's snout. Emergent: indiscretion as the inner defect that ruins outward grace.
